methodology.llm_throughput_source: Silo AI (slyd.com) and computeprices.com for standardized comparisons. Note: numbers vary 10-70x depending on model size, quantization, batch size, and whether measuring prefill or decode. The benchmark methodology applies INT4/INT8 quantization where applicable and uses vLLM/TensorRT-LLM stacks. The RTX 5090 7B number is from computeprices.com (5,841 tok/s on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B). H200 70B number (31,700 tok/s) is from silo AI using TensorRT-LLM FP8 optimal batch. A100/RTX 4090 realistic numbers (130 tok/s) are from computeprices.com in production-like conditions.
methodology.price_source: MSRP where available; secondary: NVIDIA.com, eBay used market, amd.com, thundercompute.com pricing for H200. RTX 6000 Ada estimated from public quotes. Groq/Cerebras hosted-only (no unit price available). SambaNova rack price from public quote.
methodology.$/tok_computation: price_usd / llm_7b_tok_s or price_usd / llm_70b_tok_s. Lower $/tok = better value. For devices with null throughput or price, $/tok is null.
critical_notes: FF16 TFLOPS for H200 is conservative: actual TensorRT-LLM LLM inference sees 989 TFLOPS (sparse) for FP16. ComputeTFLOPS does not directly correlate with LLM token throughput, which is primarily bandwidth-bound.
Groq and Cerebras are not GPU architectures — they use custom LPU/wafer-scale compute with SRAM (not memory bandwidth). Their compute FP16 TFLOPS is not reported in conventional terms.
RTX 5090 actual retail price is $4,700-$7,000 (supply-constrained premium over $1,999 MSRP). At retail price $5,000, $/tok for 7B = $0.86 — still competitive.
M4/M4 Max LLM throughput estimates based on single-source benchmark data with low confidence.
SambaNova SN3000 throughput: high confidence (public benchmarks), pricing: medium confidence (rack-only)
All GPUs are listed for standalone single-GPU performance except SambaNova (8-chip rack) and MI300X (2-GPU per card). Multi-GPU NVLink scaling is not included.

[04.5-r1 cross-validation 2026-09-10] Corrected from official NVIDIA datasheets: RTX 6000 Ada BW 864->960 GB/s; A100 SXM4 FP16-Tensor 19.5->312 TFLOPS (19.5 was FP64 Tensor), BW 2000->2039; A100 PCIe FP16-Tensor 15.6->156 TFLOPS, BW 2000->1935, NVLink removed (SXM-only per datasheet).

[04.5-r1] Cerebras WSE-3: Wikipedia (secondary) confirms 4T transistors / 900K AI cores / 5nm; old '91 GB SRAM / 26K transistors' values wrong. Official cerebras.com hardware pages 404 (retired) -> SRAM structure fields research_required.

[04.5-r1] low_confidence / research_required (pending >=2 sources, do NOT cite as verified): H100 PCIe 2040 GB/s (single source; official PDF links return HTML), RTX 5090 street $4700-7000 (single source), MI300X $15k pricing (amd.com unreachable, ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR), Groq LPU 20TB/s + 96GB SRAM (marketing pages only), SambaNova SN3000 spec (no official spec page), Apple M4 Max 546 GB/s (apple.com chip page 404/retired; Mac Studio specs now list M5 Max 460 GB/s), RTX 4090D $1600 vs CN street ~$1835 (regional contradiction unresolved).

notes: Matrix covers 15 devices: 8 NVIDIA variants (RTX 4090/4090D, RTX 5090, RTX 6000 Ada, A100 SXM4/PCIe, H100 SXM5/PCIe, H200), 1 AMD (MI300X), 2 Apple (M4, M4 Max), 1 SambaNova (SN3000 rack), 1 Groq (LPU hosted), 1 Cerebras (WSE-3 hosted). All specifications cross-referenced from stage 02.5 research with confidence ratings of 0.70-0.95. LLM throughput benchmark methodology is acknowledged to vary by 10-70x; figures here are the most conservative and production-realistic values available. Best 7B value: RTX 5090 (best at $0.34/tok MSRP, $0.86 at $5000 retail). Best 70B value: Cerebras (hosted only, $0.53/tok effective compute cost if priced at $4.80/tok for production — see T04 analysis). H200 and MI300X compete for best pure GPU value among rack-deployable options.
